**Reading map:** Deisenroth, Faisal & Ong, *Mathematics for Machine Learning* (2020), §2.1. This is an original lesson using our delivery-operations example—not reproduced textbook content.

## Why the concept matters

A delivery operation consumes limited resources. Suppose planning two route types requires both fuel and staff hours. The constraints must be satisfied simultaneously, not one at a time. Linear equations describe the intersection of these constraints.

## Define the mathematical relationship

$$
\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\2&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}7\\8\end{bmatrix}
$$

The displayed relationship is the main object to analyse. Specify the relevant dimensions, quantities and assumptions before using it. It should be read as a mathematical statement, not merely a programming shorthand.

## Work through an original example

From the first equation, u=7-2v. Substitute into the second: 2(7-2v)+v=8, so v=2 and u=3. The point (3,2) satisfies both equations, which is the essential check.

## What follows, and what does not

The matrix equation Ax=b is an exact feasibility problem. Some data produce no solution, some a unique solution and some infinitely many solutions. Regression later handles an inconsistent overdetermined system by seeking the closest fit.

## Test your reasoning

Replace the right-hand side by (7,7). Is the solution still unique? Verify by substitution.
